raw_text: [[File:{{{Alt}}}|28px|link=]] "Pulls Minion Prince and nearby ally units back to the deployment bar to be summoned elsewhere with extra health and Haste " Contents 1 Summary 2 Strategies 3 Statistics 4 History 5 Trivia Summary [ ] The Portal Pendant is an Epic piece of Hero Equipment for the Minion Prince that was released on October 8, 2026, within the Portal Panic Event. The Portal Pendant appears as a metal piece with two gold corners at the opposite ends with a pointed end, with a glowing emerald center. When activated, the Minion Prince pulls the nearby ally Troops , Heroes , and Pets in its area of effect back onto the Minion Prince deployment bar, allowing them to be re-deployed elsewhere (subject to the deployment zones of the village). Upon being redeployed, units gain extra health and a haste effect. Siege Machines cannot be recalled. In case the Portal Pendant cannot recall all units in its area of effect, Heroes take priority, followed by units with the highest housing space. The Minion Prince himself is exception from taking up any recall capacity, though any Pet equipped to him will still count toward the limit. Between units with the same housing space, units that were deployed first will be prioritized. For this purpose, Heroes and Pets are considered to take up 25 and 20 housing space respectively, the latter with some exceptions: If the Phoenix is still in her egg form, she will be recalled if and only if her Hero is recalled, without taking up any extra housing space. If the Angry Jelly is currently brainwashing its Hero, it will be recalled alongside its Hero without taking up housing space. Note that the Hero priority does not extend to Pets, which may be separated from their Hero if other high-housing space troops are recalled. When units are redeployed, units with the highest housing space are deployed first, with time of initial deployment being a tiebreaker between units with the same housing space. The units that are deployed also deploy in the same order as they were manually deployed. Units that are recalled will retain their current status effects that were afflicted on them when they are recalled, but prior spell effects will generally wear off since they may be redeployed outside the spell radius, and most status timers will count down while the unit is pending redeployment. Exceptions to this rule include clone lifetimes (for clones from the Clone Spell ), the Angry effect from the Angry Jelly and Angry Spell , active Hero Equipment effect timers (such as Rage Vial and Eternal Tome ), and revival timers (for Heroes being temporarily revived by Phoenix), all of which are paused while pending redeployment. In addition to the ability, it grants additional hitpoints to the Minion Prince, and also increases the amount of health he recovers when using the ability.
